page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1.7xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 33 MB of L3 cache and supports hardware-assisted technologies such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX and AVX-512F). It is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.0 GB per core, and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks reveal a clear distinction between single-threaded and multi-threaded capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by bottom 25% scores in stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests, alongside a bottom 10% result in single-threaded gzip compression. Conversely, multi-core execution scales to average levels, with stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all placing in the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate average throughput for both cached and uncached operations, though the overall PassMark memory score remains in the bottom 25%.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and lack of local storage, the ecs.sn1.7xlarge is structured for compute-heavy workloads that scale horizontally across multiple threads rather than relying on single-core speed. It is suited for multi-threaded batch processing, static web serving, and moderate database operations, where its average multi-core performance can be utilized. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a high density of dedicated vCPUs relative to memory, making it a viable option for parallelized workloads that do not require massive memory footprints or local solid-state storage.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1.7xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor at 2.5 GHz. Operating under the KVM hypervisor, this server lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. Benchmark data indicates a performance tradeoff: single-core metrics and single-threaded compression are weak, placing in the bottom 25% and 10% respectively, while multi-core operations, Redis SET throughput, and static web serving achieve average tier performance. With a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for parallelized, compute-bound tasks rather than memory-intensive applications. It is best suited for multi-threaded batch processing, web serving, and distributed database operations.
